What's New in v1.2.0

  • 📝 Description: macOS 27 Golden Gate support, a cleaner interface, editable layouts, history previews, and more reliable Dock switching.
  • ✨ New: Ready for macOS 27 Golden Gate – full support for the latest macOS release.
  • ✨ New: Customize layouts while creating them. Start with your current Dock, then add, remove, or rearrange apps, folders, and spacers before saving.
  • ✨ New: Edit layouts you’ve already saved. Save your changes without touching your current Dock, then apply the layout when you’re ready to switch.
  • ✨ New: Choose how each layout handles running apps: follow the global Auto-Quit Apps setting, always quit apps outside the layout, or keep them open.
  • ✨ New: Layout History now shows what changed during a switch before you restore your previous Dock.
  • ✨ New: Apple Shortcuts support – choose and apply a saved layout with Shortcuts or Automations.
  • 📈 Improvements: Slightly redesigned and cleaner main window. History, Settings, and New Layout have moved from the sidebar to the toolbar, leaving more room for your layouts.
  • 📈 Improvements: Exported layouts are easier to use on another Mac. Modoki finds installed apps, flags missing items, and still accepts older backups.
  • 📈 Improvements: Click a layout in sidebar to view it, or double-click to apply it.
  • 📈 Improvements: You can now see progress while a layout is being applied.
  • 📈 Improvements: Better handling of Dock restarts and Focus Mode changes behind the scenes.
  • 🛠️ Fix: Fixed rapid switching sometimes showing a Dock command error or reverting to the previous layout.
  • 🛠️ Fix: Updated keyboard shortcuts, now they're reliable again.
  • 🛠️ Fix: Layout History now shows the correct before-and-after changes, making it clear what Undo will restore.
  • 🛠️ Fix: Fixed a crash when removing several spacers from the Dock.
  • 🛠️ Fix: Multiple minor internal fixes and improvements.
  • ⚠️ Compatibility: Modoki now requires macOS 15 or later. If you use macOS 14, stay on v1.1.0.

Known Issues

  • If “Show dock icon” is turned off and you open Modoki through Spotlight, its Dock icon may remain after you close the window.
